reviews.title: Perfect gaming case if you need 5.25" drives.
reviews.comment: First PC build since a Vista machine, cases are not just cases anymore so I was worried a little. I wanted an external 5.25 for PS2/3 emulation(plus I'm old), in a simple, sleek, modern design. This case checked all the boxes. Not a case/cord routing expert but I had no problem making everything fit while looking clean and tidy. The Thermalright PS120 fit with some room to spare. You could probably buy better, but if this checks all your boxes, get it and put your extra money elsewhere. Been running close to 2 months now and I can't see the case having any issues post-install. Under full stress the CPU runs 60F and GPU 70F, airflow seems good. Build: X670E Tomahawk, 9800x3d, 64G Corsair CL30 6K, Phantom Spirit 120, Nitro+ 7900xtx, A1000GL, 4-140mm, 5-120mm + 2-120mm CPU fans, Blu-ray RW, and 5.25 USB-C 3.2 expansion. Room for multiple PCIe cards(covers are replaceable), or front 240 cooler, 280 may not fit. Max fan config seems to be 6-140mm(2top, 2bottom, 2front) and 1-120mm(rear), but I do not think you can fit 2 on the bottom due to the PSU, I can't. I have zero complaints about this case.
reviews.author: WA_Wanderer

reviews.title: Quality case will hold anything
reviews.comment: This case will fit a single Xeon server board without a problem, it’s built well and the mini has served for every desktop I have built for last year or so. Airflow is great and enough room to run power supply wires on the back side for a clean build AND it has 2 large bays for media centers or dvd’s or anything you like.
reviews.author: D G

reviews.title: Retro old style case?
reviews.comment: Needed a case for my older computer (amd fx 8350) for my old graphics card that was too long for my old case. Been looking at this one for a few months. Cable management wise I had to remove the HDD bay to fit some of the cables in. It doesn't look perfect but it works. The free front fans are nice. I had a spare 180mm fan for the back. The case is very lightweight. The front drive bays which you don't find anymore on most modern cases was great for my old dvd drive. The main panel to open the case doesn't slide in easily. The case screws are weird, you screw it in and it doesn't tighten, then when you go to unscrew it, it tightens. I think it's due to the little springs on the screws. Frustrating, the screws have to be perfectly straight to get it to screw in. It has dust filters and room for a little improvement like a water cooled fan if I want to. Overall this serves my needs and is 50x better than my old case.
